title: SaTeen: Learning Structural Alignment for Continual Test-Time Adaptation
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Test data keeps two stable structural priors: dominant features within each sample and a shared low-dimensional manifold across samples.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, heatmap photo beside manifold scatter
description: Two side-by-side panels with large titles above each. Panel (a), 'Intra-Sample Structure', is a close-up photo of a cat's face with a rainbow Grad-CAM-style heatmap on top. Red and orange mark the eye and forehead region, and the colors cool to blue over the background, which has a house, a window and a fridge. This shows that the dominant, discriminative features stay stable. Panel (b), 'Inter-Sample Structure', is a bordered 2-D scatter plot of blue dots forming a wavy, snake-like S-shaped curve. Its legend reads 'Source Manifold'. The dots show the intrinsic manifold that test data stays close to. The eye goes first to the bright heatmap, then to the large blue manifold. There are no arrows, modules or text annotations.
caption: (a) Illustration of intra-sample structure, such as shapes, which is usually held in TTA. (b) Illustration of inter-sample structure, i.e. intrinsic manifold, to which test data is generally close. Considering both priors can boost model adaptation smoothly.
abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) aims to reconcile model generalization in the presence of distribution shifts. Current TTA methods usually leverage sample uncertainty to select reliable samples for model adjustment via entropy minimization (EM). However, sample uncertainty often relies on a plausible metric and leaves many unreliable samples into EM process, potentially leading to model collapse. Importantly, these excluded samples incur biased data features of the shifted distribution in TTA. This paper introduces SaTeen, a S tructural A lignment-based Te st-Tim e Adaptatio n method that performs two-fold aligning the structures of test samples with the reliable reference structures. Specifically, the two-fold alignments are 1) Intra-sample structure alignment, where SaTeen maximizes cross-entropy discrepancy between a sample (reference) and its structure-disrupted counterpart, with the assumption of stable dominant features; 2) Inter-sample structure alignment, where SaTeen minimizes the reconstruction error of test samples in the reference subspace spanned by the Incremental PCA on reliable samples, with the assumption of stale intrinsic data manifold. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that SaTeen achieves the state-of-the-art performance across various scenarios for both TTA and continual TTA.
